references.text: God gave Moses the two stone tablets of the testimony, written with God's finger, which are the first tablets mentioned in Exodus 34:1.
Describes the first stone tablets that Moses brought down from the mountain, written on both sides by God Himself.
Moses broke the first tablets at the foot of the mountain when he saw the golden calf, explaining the need for new tablets in Exodus 34:1.
Moses recounts how the Lord told him to carve two new stone tablets and how God wrote the ten words on them, just as on the first tablets.
Confirms that there was nothing else in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses placed there at Horeb.
Paul refers to the stone tablets and contrasts them with the writing of the new covenant on the fleshly tablets of the heart.
Mentions the ark of the covenant which contained the stone tablets with the words of the covenant.
Describes the same event (carving of new tablets) from two different narrative perspectives.
Complementary text that completes the action described in the source verse (writing and storage of the new tablets).
Contrast between God's judgment on a stiff-necked people and His grace in restoring the covenant.
Highlights the significance of the new tablets being 'like the first' by describing the divine origin of the original tablets.
